title: Don't. Laugh.
idea: Potato Desk 14: you laughed in court again; one more laugh is ten years and you must not look at the judge's head. Your best friend testifies (fart chair, helium oath, your bowl-cut school photo, a snot bubble); you hold it. The judge stands: a steaming hash-brown toupee with a bite missing. You hold it; the jury laughs: ten years each.

hook.what: a judge, his head cut off at the eyebrows by the frame top, slams his gavel at you; your lawyer beside you

props.staged: panels fixed to the back wall
on a block on the bench's riser, hidden by the bench

captions.text: You laughed in my courtroom. Not once. But *TWICE.*
One more, it's ten years. So here's my advice:
Keep your face still, and whatever you do...
*DON'T* look at his head. It's too dangerous for you.
Why? What's on his head?
The most dangerous thing. Eyes down, like I said.
Defense, your witness. Let's get this done.
Your Honor, his best friend. The most serious one.
Oh no.
A smile is *five* years. A giggle is *ten.*
Now raise your right hand. And swear it. And then...
I swear to tell the truth, the whole truth, *amen!*
Think sad thoughts. Think rain. Think tax.
Is he a serious man? Just give me the facts.
The most serious man that I've ever known.
*Exhibit A:* his serious face. Fully grown.
Did he ever laugh at something... he shouldn't?
At your head? Oh, he *NEVER!* I mean... he couldn't!
Case dismissed. You are free to go.
I... held it.
All of you? *TEN YEARS. EACH.* Told you so.
